title: Alisal school district won't rename César E. Chávez Elementary

 alisal school district to discuss process of renaming cesar chavez elementary Advertisement Updated: 5:18 PM PST Nov 19, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Josh Copitch Assistant News Director Alisal school district won't rename César E. Chávez Elementary
 Updated: 5:18 PM PST Nov 19, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Josh Copitch Assistant News Director SALINAS, Calif. — Alisal Union School District Board of Trustees will not be renaming César E. Chávez Elementary School after they say the community didn't want the change. 
 On Wednesday, the board voted to dissolve the citizens committee created to explore a name change. The vote was 4-0 with Leticia Garcia absent. 
 Advertisement The committee only held one meeting where a quorum was met. During that meeting, they requested a district survey on whether the name should be changed. The results were as follows: 
 Chávez staff: Change the name: Yes: 62%. No: 38%
 Chávez community: Change the name: Yes: 32%. No 68%
 Chávez students: Change the name: Yes: 70%. No: 30% 
 Alisal USD community: Change the name: Yes: 34% No: 66%
 Between all the surveys, only 43% of respondents wanted to change the name of the school. 
 “The saddest thing would be to ignore the 56 percent who said to leave it alone,” she said. “It took time to set up surveys, it took time for people to respond and now we’re responding to our community. We are going to listen to the Alisal staff. At the moment, the community has spoken with 56 percent (of the vote) and we want to honor that," said Board President Guadalupe Gilpas Barrera during the Wednesday night board meeting.
